fixes.explanation: A cloud, baker! Moses finishes the work in verse 33, and then the cloud comes down over the Tent of Meeting. The verse says “…the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” After all those bases, frames and crossbars, that's what the whole project was waiting for. I bet Moses just stood there taking it in.

A storm is a fair guess, friend, but the verse names a cloud. It covers the Tent of Meeting, and the text says “…the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” A cloud settles on the tent, and that's the picture the verse gives us.

Wind is a fair guess, friend, but the text names a cloud. It covers the Tent of Meeting, and then “…the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” Moses had just finished the work (Exodus 40:33), and verse 35 says the cloud had settled on the tent. Wind blows through and moves on, but this cloud settled.

You've got the right month, friend, but the day is different. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “On the first day of the first month you are to set up the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.” So the day is the very first, not the tenth. That's nine days of difference, and you can bake a LOT of cookies in nine days.

Holy is the word. The LORD says to Moses, Israel's leader, “Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; consecrate it along with all its furnishings, and it shall be holy.” The oil goes on, and the whole place and everything in it is set apart. Nothing in there gets skipped.

Water it is. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.” Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). Before the garments and the anointing, there's a washing. Think of it like clean hands before you touch the dough.

Oil is in this passage, friend, but it's not the washing. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to bring Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and his sons to the entrance and “…wash them with water.” The anointing comes after, in the verses that follow. Water first, then oil.

No wine in this scene, friend. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to bring Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and his sons to the entrance and “…wash them with water.” Plain water, nothing fancy. Even in my bakery, the thing that gets used for washing up is water.

That's the reason the LORD gives. He tells Moses, Israel's leader, to clothe Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), with the holy garments, anoint him and consecrate him “…so that he may serve Me as a priest.” The garments and the oil are for service. I think that makes it a pretty big job.

Battle isn't mentioned here, friend. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to clothe Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), with the holy garments, anoint him and consecrate him “…so that he may serve Me as a priest.” The reason the LORD gives is priestly service.

Judging disputes isn't in this passage, friend. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to clothe Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), with the holy garments, anoint him and consecrate him “…so that he may serve Me as a priest.” The reason the LORD gives is priesthood. That's the whole answer.

Offerings do show up in this chapter, friend. Moses offers the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar in verse 29. But for the lifting cloud, the text says “Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out through all the stages of their journey.” That's what they do: they set out.

Gathering to hear Moses is a fair guess, friend, but in these verses the cloud is the signal. When it lifts, the Israelites set out. Verse 37 adds that if it was not lifted, they would not set out until the day it was taken up. I bet everybody kept one eye on that cloud.
